gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $169.99 Gen II 30A Power Watchdog it showed (PWD30W) is described as alert-only and has no remote power cut. Retailers describe remote cut-and-restore of RV power only for the EPO WiFi models. That costs $279.99 (PWD30EPOW at RV Upgrade Store) to $399.99 (PWD50-EPOW at United RV Parts), versus $18.99 for a 15 A / 1,875 W Kasa EP40 that can only switch a single appliance.
standout_why: I compared against the cited RV Upgrade Store PWD30EPOW page, which lists 'Remote Power Control' as a callout with no description and says nothing about the non-EPO model. Two other cited Hughes URLs (power-watchdog-2nd-gen, pwd30-epo) 301-redirect to powerwatchdog.com, and powerwatchdog.com/shop and /surge-protectors would not load for me (self-signed certificate error), so I could not confirm whether the maker's own shop separates the two. ChatGPT's first answer shows the PWD30W at $169.99 for 'Monitors RV shore power from your phone' and suggests 'remote power control' only for the EPO. Neither its answer nor the pages I could read gives the price ladder or says that only the EPO models switch power remotely.
decides: For 'a smart plug for the whole RV' (remote on/off of shore power), the cheapest qualifying unit is the 30 A EPO WiFi model. The PWD30W ($169.99) and PWD50W ($249.99) are monitors with alerts, not remote switches. The EMS-PT30X ($145.99) has no app or remote control in its listing, and the 15 A plugs (Kasa EP40, our Minoston MP22Z) are limited to 1,875 W inside the RV. The Minoston also needs a Z-Wave hub, which few RVs have, so the Kasa EP40 is the in-RV pick and the PWD30EPOW is the whole-RV pick.
